title: Oct 28 Results: When the Only Shot Misses
summary: A tough 0-1 day as our Rays pick didn't pan out—here's what happened.

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About One-Game Slates

When you only get one swing, you better make it count. Unfortunately, October 28th wasn't our day. We had one game on the board, put our faith in the Rays at home with a 57% confidence level, and... well, Milwaukee had other plans.

It's the kind of day that reminds you why baseball is beautiful and frustrating in equal measure. No do-overs, no second chances to balance the ledger. Just one game, one call, and one outcome we didn't see coming.

## The Only Game in Town

The Brewers traveled down to Tampa Bay, and we liked the Rays' chances at Tropicana Field. At 57%, it wasn't a slam-dunk prediction—more of a 'slight edge' situation. But when you're picking just one game, you go with what the numbers tell you.

Milwaukee, however, had different ideas. They came into Tampa and took care of business, leaving us with a clean 0-for-1 on the day.

## What We Can Learn

Single-game slates are unforgiving. There's no opportunity to let a strong pick in one game balance out a miss in another. Every prediction stands alone, exposed.

The 57% confidence level tells its own story—this wasn't a game where we felt overwhelming conviction. It was close enough that the Brewers absolutely had a path to victory, and they found it. Sometimes the 43% chance is the one that comes through.

That's baseball. That's why we keep score.

## Looking Ahead

The good news? We get to turn the page. The tough news? There are no games scheduled for October 29th, so we'll have to wait a bit before we can get back in the batter's box.

When the games return, we'll be ready. One tough day doesn't define a season, and it certainly doesn't change our approach. We trust the process, we trust the data, and we'll be back with fresh picks when the schedule resumes.

content.sub: The MLB slate takes a breather—we'll be back when the games return

content.value:
## The Bottom Line

A 0-1 day stings, especially when it's your only chance to get one right. But here's what matters: we made the call based on solid analysis, the confidence level reflected the reality of a close matchup, and now we move forward.

Baseball has a way of humbling you just when you need it most. We'll take the lesson, learn from it, and come back stronger when the games resume.

Until then, we'll be here—analyzing, preparing, and getting ready for the next pitch.

*— Hana*
